subject: Meteorology
title: De-Icing and Anti-Icing
description: A fast breakdown of De-Icing and Anti-Icing for builders.

hook.text: Aircraft fight ice with two strategies—de-icing removes ice that's already formed; anti-icing prevents it from forming.

buildup.text: Pneumatic boots on props and smaller aircraft inflate to crack ice off wing leading edges—a mechanical solution.

discovery.text: Heated leading edges called thermal anti-ice systems use bleed air from jet engines to keep surfaces warm.

twist.text: Ground de-icing sprays heated glycol fluid on the aircraft before takeoff—creating a temporary protective film.

climax.text: The holdover time of de-icing fluid is limited—if takeoff is delayed too long, the aircraft must be de-iced again.

punchline.text: Fight ice before it forms—or crack it off after. Both save lives.

quiz.question: What is holdover time?
options: How long de-icing fluid remains effective
